title: Famous News Anchor Jon Snow Says He Has Alzheimer's — and He's Still Reporting!
summary: Imagine hearing a secret that you're scared to tell anyone. That's what happened to Jon Snow, a famous news presenter in the UK. For 32 years, people watched him on Channel 4 News. Now, at age 78, he has told the world he has Alzheimer's disease. Alzheimer's is an illness that makes it harder to remember things and think clearly over time. At first, Jon didn't want anyone to know. He said in a new film, "At the beginning I wanted to hide it, there's so much prejudice. Any sort of hint of mental decay, you're sort of dead." But he also said the disease is not something he feels all day, every day. "There are moments when it pops up but it's not an all day every day condition, and that's what I cling onto," he said. His wife, Precious Lunga, helped him see a doctor in 2023. He took a memory test and got 29 out of 30 — almost perfect! But a brain scan later showed he had Alzheimer's. Now Jon is speaking out to help others. He said, "If I don't speak out, who will?" He even made a documentary called Jon Snow: A Last Big Story. In it, he investigates an environmental disaster in Zambia. The film will be on TV on June 20. The UK Prime Minister called Jon "a true giant in journalism" who is now helping people feel less alone.
why_it_matters: This story shows that even people we admire on TV face tough health problems, and being open about them can make others feel less alone.

background_read: Jon Snow is a well-known British journalist who presented the evening news on Channel 4 (a popular TV news program in the UK) for more than three decades.
Alzheimer's disease affects millions of people around the world, especially older adults, and scientists are still searching for a cure.
The UK Prime Minister (the leader of the United Kingdom) often speaks publicly about important issues and praised Jon for his bravery.
Article_Structure: WHO: Jon Snow, a famous UK news presenter for Channel 4 News.
WHAT: He announced that he has Alzheimer's disease and made a documentary about an environmental disaster in Zambia.
WHERE: In the United Kingdom, where his show Channel 4 News is broadcast.
WHY: To speak out against prejudice and help others with Alzheimer's feel less alone.

perspectives.description: Jon believes that talking about his Alzheimer's helps fight the unfair judgment people with the disease often face. He wants to show that life can still have purpose.
Some people might think that a person with memory problems should stop working, because they worry he could make mistakes on live TV. This shows the stigma Jon wants to break.
Doctors know that Alzheimer's progresses slowly and people can still function well for years. Early diagnosis and support from family can help maintain a good quality of life.
